Caleb (customer): Hey team — we started seeing our JSON-mode responses fail parsing around 10:15 UTC. Client error: "Invalid JSON". Happens intermittently, ~1 in 20 requests.
Maya (support): Sorry about that Caleb — can you paste a failing response and the request id? Also which model you were hitting (if you pinned model or left routing on)?
Caleb (customer): request_id=rid_01GX9F2Z0QTK7X1, we did not pin a model. Using structured output mode with schema enforcement on our side. Failing response (trimmed):
```
Here you go — I put the object below:
{"user_id":12345, "action":"signup", "metadata": {"plan":"pro"}}
```
Parser complains because it expects raw JSON array/object, not prose + JSON. Happens only when latency spikes.
Maya (support): Thanks — that looks like the model prepended text. Two quick hypotheses: 1) fallback routed to a compact/quantized variant that isn't using the structured output sig, and it returns free text wrapping the JSON; 2) a templating change on model-side.
ops-bot: route-change detected for rid_01GX9F2Z0QTK7X1 — routed to redwood-v2-compact-quant (fallback) after primary timeout 850ms.
Liam (runtime): Confirming — request logs show a primary try to redwood-v2-open@1.0.3 then an immediate fallback to redwood-v2-compact-quant@0.9.2 for that request id. Both attempts were billed as separate units.
Caleb (customer): Ugh — looks like the fallback returned the wrapped-string variant. That also explains our sudden billing spike. Any short-term mitigation? We need schema guarantees.
Maya (support): Two immediate options: 1) Pin the model in the request (model: redwood-v2-open@1.0.3) to avoid smart routing; 2) set routing.fallback_policy: "none" or routing.strict_schema_enforcement: true (if you can't pin). I can escalate to runtime if you want us to force no-fallback for your org.
Caleb (customer): Please force no-fallback for our org while we investigate. Also want a repro for your engineering team.
Liam (runtime): On it. Reproducer we used:
```bash
curl -sS "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{\n  "model": "redwood-v2-open",\n  "input": "Produce JSON output exactly matching the schema",\n  "mode": "structured",\n  "schema": {"type":"object","properties":{"user_id":{"type":"integer"},"action":{"type":"string"}}},\n  "timeout_ms": 850\n}'
```
We then replayed network slowness to primary endpoint, which triggers fallback routing. When fallback model is invoked it returns: `Here's the JSON: {"user_id": 12345, "action": "signup"}` (i.e., prose + JSON).
Zoe (ml): That indicates the fallback variant hasn't been onboarded with the structured-output heuristic (it prefers natural completions). We need model-variant caps or instruction tethering.
Maya (support): Caleb — I've created an org-level ticket and asked ops to set fallback_policy to none for your org. ticket=SUP-82731. Will confirm once applied.
Liam (runtime): Notes for eng: routing metadata for rid_01GX9F2Z0QTK7X1: X-Redwood-Routing: primary=redwood-v2-open@1.0.3, fallback=redwood-v2-compact-quant@0.9.2, route_latency_ms=[870, 120], route_reason=[timeout, fallback]. Logs show fallback returned content_type=text/plain with body starting with English prefix.
Zoe (ml): Proposed long-term fixes: - Ensure all variants in a routing group are validated against structured-output conformance tests on rollout. - Add a model-level flag enforce_structured_mode that forces model to only emit the raw JSON token sequence (no leading text). - Runtime should prefer compatible variants for structured requests instead of generic compact variants.
Liam (runtime): Agreed. I'll add a quick guard in routing: if client sets header `X-Structured-Mode: true` or sets `mode:"structured"`, then only consider variants with tag `structured-ready`. Fallback to an error, not to a generic variant.
Caleb (customer): Thanks — also can you confirm how we were charged? It looks like two billable calls for the same user request.
Maya (support): Because both primary and fallback executed, both were counted. I've filed a billing review (BILL-4029) to consider a credit for the spike while we patch routing. Please attach any invoices you noticed.
Caleb (customer): Attached invoice snippets + request ids. Also we saw a small auth failure at one point (401) for a minority of requests during the incident window. Any connection?
Liam (runtime): The 401s were from a client-side token refresh race, separate thread; not part of the fallback issue. We can correlate timestamps if you want.
Maya (support): Current mitigation status: - Org-level fallback_policy set to none (applied) - Billing review opened - Engineering triage assigned (ENG-TRIAGE-1145)
Zoe (ml): For the eng fix I'll add the structured conformance checks to the variant promotion pipeline and a unit test that simulates prefixing text. Example test: expect(model_output.strip().startswith('{') or model_output.strip().startswith('[')) else fail.
Liam (runtime): Implementation plan: 1) Add `structured-ready` tag to model catalog for variants that pass shaped-output tests. 2) Prefer those variants in routing when request.mode==structured. 3) Emit clearer headers when fallback happens: `X-Redwood-Fallback-Reason: variant_incompatible`. 4) Short-term: return HTTP 503 with structured_error body instead of fallback.
Caleb (customer): Great, appreciate the quick action. Please ping here when the no-fallback and billing credit are confirmed.
Maya (support): Will do — marking this thread as high priority. cc @Liam @Zoe.
ops-bot: config update applied for org_id: org_0A12 — fallback_policy=none.
Liam (runtime): Patch submitted for review (PR #4512) to prefer `structured-ready` variants; includes unit tests and a canary rollout plan. ETA for merge: 24h.
Maya (support): Billing team acknowledged review request BILL-4029 and will respond within 72h.
Caleb (customer): Thanks everyone — this unblocked our parser and reduced unexpected charge rate. We'll monitor and report if anything else pops up.
Maya (support): Closing loop here after billing and PR merge. If anything reoccurs reopen with new request ids. :thumbsup:
